reason: Execution transactions took one global advisory key exclusively, so every project's worker SQL ran one at a time. They now hold that key shared plus an exclusive per-runtime key; the first shared-row write takes a schema-qualified shared-row writer key; StoreTransaction rereads shared rows under it and gains lock_shared_rows (used by the Butler global check); the host Work batch keeps the key exclusive but checks readiness without it (and without row locks). Per-id single-integer advisory keys (operation, run, Butler session, workspace provenance, project name) move off the execution key's value through advisory_keys.per_id_key, and the Work batch also checks owner fence preconditions without the key. Selected: the new PostgreSQL race tests (including a real colliding operation id and the real Butler global-check race) (test_execution_locks: concurrency, same-runtime serialization, ownership-row ordering, shared-row writes, stale rows, opposite-order writes, read-then-write, cross-project writes, Work batch exclusion, ownership change, handoff, raw writes, SQLite no-op), the execution scope and coordination contracts, Work batches (including the new waiting-batch test), deployment handoff lifecycle, handoff admission and participants, the execution worker, store transactions, storage integrations (ingest) and Butler instructions (global check). Selecting test_runtime_coordination provisions the CI PostgreSQL database for the PostgreSQL variants. Rebased onto 3c0481c: test_runtime_work_batches keeps main's #1028/#1001 worker admission and retirement tests (an earlier rebase had dropped them) and #1062's idle grace tests, and adds the parametrized waiting-batch test (no advisory or row lock while a batch waits).
exclusions: Tests that fail identically on pristine origin/main are not selected: test_butler_instructions::test_global_check_uses_saved_butler_harness_effort, test_butler_sessions::test_reservation_api_is_project_scoped_and_reuses_active_session, five test_setup tests (event-loop responsiveness, concurrent scratch creation, interrupted migration, setup status contract, image preparation) and test_workspace_provenance::test_large_unchanged_checkout_shares_chunks_and_queries_only_compact_index, and test_execution_worker::test_idle_worker_makes_no_fenced_claims_and_still_picks_up_work, whose PostgreSQL variant sees a FOR SHARE read of runtime_processes in its idle window on pristine origin/main (22b46bf, 4 of 4 local runs) as on this branch; the rest of those files, which exercise the per-id advisory key callers, is selected by node id. SQLite variants of the PostgreSQL-only lock tests skip by design. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. The scratch-Core load A/B, statement captures and the independent subagent reviews are recorded in the PR, not executed by CI. test_setup.py's per-id caller cases are not selected either: run together in one process they pass (19 of 19), but a non-daemon aiosqlite connection thread is left behind, so pytest never exits after its summary. CI run 43644922734 on d33ecb7 sat in its Test step for 30+ minutes and was cancelled, and a local run with CI's flags stayed alive 600 s after pytest.main returned 0. The same lingering exit happens on pristine origin/main (22b46bf) locally. The shared per_id_key helper the setup project-name lock uses stays covered by test_execution_locks.
